title: Weather and lightning
summary: If you can hear thunder, you are in danger: get inside a building or hard-topped vehicle.

list: Tall, growing cumulus clouds on a summer morning mean heavy rain and thunderstorms are possible later in the day. In the mountains, storms typically build in the early afternoon: plan to be down by noon.

Clouds that lower and thicken can mean a warm front is coming, with several hours of rain. A line of thunderstorms can sweep through just ahead of a cold front; after it passes, the wind shifts and the temperature drops.

blocks.cap: Count the seconds from flash to thunder and divide by 5 for the distance in miles.

list: If you can hear thunder, you are in danger. Get inside a substantial building or a hard-topped vehicle with the windows closed. Tents, sheds and picnic shelters don’t protect you. Lightning can strike as far as 10 miles from the rain.
No place outside is safe. If you’re caught out, get off hills, ridges and peaks and away from lone tall trees, water and metal. Never lie flat on the ground. In a group, spread out.
Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back out.
